sub.en: Look at the sentences. Which word means you are fairly sure, and which one means you are not?

items.q: I think electric cars ___ cheaper than petrol ones by 2030.
items.why: will = you think it is likely. might = it is possible, but you are not sure. The verb after both stays in the base form.

items.q: Flying taxis ___ arrive, but I doubt it.
I ___ think people will stop driving completely.
items.why: English puts the negative on “think”, not on “will”: I don’t think it will happen.

acts.title: What we will actually be doing in 2045
text: Every ten years somebody predicts that we will all be flying to work, and every ten years we are still in the same traffic jam. It is worth asking why the predictions keep failing.

The honest answer is that transport changes slowly, because it is expensive and because it is built into the shape of cities. The Tokyo–Osaka high-speed line will extend in 2045 and it will cost around fifty-one billion dollars; the trains will float above the track rather than run on it, which sounds like science fiction and is in fact forty-year-old technology finally arriving.

So what will change? Fuel, almost certainly. Electric cars will be cheaper than petrol ones well before 2035, and cities that have already built cycle lanes will have quieter, greener centres than those that have not. Buses might become free in some cities — three have tried it and none of them has gone back.

And what will not change? The traffic jam. More roads produce more cars; this has been true since the 1960s and nothing in the next twenty years will make it untrue. We might travel more cheaply and more quietly. We will probably not travel any faster.

write.q: Predict how people in your city will travel in twenty years: 6 sentences. Two with will, two with might, one negative with “I don’t think … will”, and one thing you are sure will not change.
write.model: In twenty years I think most cars here will be electric, because petrol ones will simply be too expensive to run. The city might finally finish the cycle lanes it started in 2018. Buses might become free — three cities have tried it and none of them went back. I don’t think people will stop using cars completely; the winter here is eight months long. The metro will probably be longer, and it will still be full at half past eight. The traffic jam on the main road will not change at all.

speak.q: Make four predictions out loud about transport in your city: two with will, one with might, and one with “I don’t think … will”.
speak.model: I think most cars will be electric in twenty years. The metro will probably be longer. Buses might become free. I don’t think people will stop driving here — it’s too cold for half the year.
